findings.reason: the plan's cause is "the place, not the merge", and a pull is such a merge, so a guard that recognises only the `git merge` verb leaves the most common way a coordinator updates the shared checkout able to reproduce the incident the plan cites.
findings.text: the new rule is scoped to a `git merge` command, yet the shared checkout has `pull.rebase=false` (measured with `git config --get pull.rebase`), so an ordinary `git pull --no-rebase origin <branch>` runs a merge in the installed tree and writes the same conflict markers the plan exists to prevent

findings.reason: a fail-open arm is exactly where such a rule silently switches itself off, and without a case that separates exit 1 from an error exit the gate cannot show which path it proved, so an implementation that fails open on every non-zero prediction would pass the node's whole measure.
findings.text: the done-when asserts the conflicting arm is denied and the clean and linked-worktree arms are allowed, but asserts nothing about the arm the Deliverable declares for a prediction that cannot answer (an unknown revision), and it does not require the test to show a conflict exit is distinguished from a prediction error exit

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor resolves: `2bafddb13` is `fix(crew): prove a follower's replacement imports before it reloads` (2026-09-25), `a44b5105f` resolves to a 2026-10-08 commit, the recovery split landed as promote `ba21415ea8` at 19:04:27 on 2026-10-08 matching "merged at 19:04", `reckon/crew/recovery.py` and `reckon/hooks/worker_git_guard.py` both exist, and the guard is registered as a `PreToolUse`/`Bash` hook in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so "already registered ... for every session" is true and the scope claim "applies only inside a crew run" matches `decide()`'s early return on a missing `RECKON_RUN_ID`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's done-when exercises the conflict, clean and linked-worktree arms but never the "the prediction cannot answer" arm its own Deliverable declares, and it never states how an exit-1 conflict is told from an error exit.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate is a committed test under `tests/`, the negative control is logged into the run record, and nothing in the plan writes evidence to a scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test name and the rule are named for what they do (`test_merge_guard_refuses_a_conflicting_merge.py`), and no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a path, symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause matches the cited evidence and the stated mechanism does produce the done-when: I ran `git merge-tree --write-tree --no-messages HEAD side` on git 2.39.3 in a conflicting scratch repository and it printed the three stage lines for `f.txt` (so the conflicted path is available despite `--no-messages`) and exited 1; but the rule is scoped to the `git merge` verb while the shared checkout's own pull policy performs merges too.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 has one deliverable (one new refusal rule in the existing guard), one test file, and one negative control; the docstring sentence is part of that same rule, not a second one.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan declares `plan-standalone` and no section carries a link; the sprint item in `docs/sprints/S25.html` repeats the same done-when slug, and no plan or section under `docs/` declares a dependency on `a-merge-never-breaks-the-installed-tree`, so nothing it needs is missing and no relationship points at the wrong node.
